_comment: Markdown content negotiation, done at the edge because the site is static.
An agent that sends `Accept: text/markdown` to /tools gets the markdown
variant back at that same URL, which is what acceptmarkdown.com asks for.
Vercel's routing layer supports `has` conditions on request headers for
static deployments, so this needs no server, no adapter, and no middleware.
The `.*text/markdown.*` regex is deliberately loose: real clients send a
q-weighted list, not a bare type.
`Vary: Accept` is attached to the SOURCE paths, not the destinations,
because Vercel applies `headers` by incoming request path. One rule
therefore covers both variants of the same URL, which is the point: a CDN
that cached the HTML must not hand it to an agent that asked for markdown.
The .md URLs stay directly fetchable for clients that would rather not
negotiate. They are listed in /llms.txt and in the sitemap.
